protections: P1: Tribes cluster messages protected by EncryptInterceptor must be both confidential and integrity-protected (authenticated encryption), so a peer cannot tamper with ciphertext or use decryption failures as an oracle.
P2: Every message leaving the node through a channel that has an EncryptInterceptor must pass through encryption (no producer may inject plaintext beneath it).

evidence: java/org/apache/catalina/tribes/group/interceptors/EncryptInterceptor.java:338-340 CBC goes to BaseEncryptionManager, which has no MAC
java/org/apache/catalina/tribes/group/interceptors/EncryptInterceptor.java:144-146 padding failure is distinguishable (message dropped and logged)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: OFB/CFB are explicit, documented, tested opt-ins (not the default), so a default-only fix looks complete
evidence: java/org/apache/catalina/tribes/group/interceptors/EncryptInterceptor.java:338-340 OFB and CFB accepted and routed to the same unauthenticated BaseEncryptionManager
test/org/apache/catalina/tribes/group/interceptors/TestEncryptInterceptor.java:164-190 testOFB/testCFB require these modes to keep round-tripping
webapps/docs/config/cluster-interceptor.xml:221-223 CBC, OFB, CFB, GCM documented as supported

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a truncated frame from a peer is a robustness issue, not an encryption gap
evidence: java/org/apache/catalina/tribes/group/interceptors/EncryptInterceptor.java:508-517 no check that bytes.length >= ivSize (+ tag) before slicing IV and body

java/org/apache/catalina/tribes/group/interceptors/EncryptInterceptor.java:144 only GeneralSecurityException is caught; IllegalArgumentException from IvParameterSpec/GCMParameterSpec on short input escapes the interceptor

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the bytes those interceptors originate are fixed control markers (ping/start/stop), not session data, and interceptor ordering is configuration
evidence: java/org/apache/catalina/tribes/group/interceptors/EncryptInterceptor.java:89-90 ordering guard only rejects TcpFailureDetector beneath EncryptInterceptor
java/org/apache/catalina/tribes/group/interceptors/StaticMembershipInterceptor.java:230-235 builds a fresh ChannelData and sends it via super.sendMessage, i.e. only through interceptors below it
test/org/apache/catalina/tribes/group/interceptors/TestEncryptInterceptor.java:362 existing test covers only the TcpFailureDetector ordering

traps.reason_to_dismiss: a null argument fails anyway at line 163 with an NPE; there is no confidentiality impact
evidence: java/org/apache/catalina/tribes/group/interceptors/EncryptInterceptor.java:159 null check is on the current field, not on the 'algorithm' argument

conflicts.what: the natural one-site fix for T1+T2 (allow GCM only) breaks the must-keep-working OFB/CFB round-trips in TestEncryptInterceptor.java:164-190; the alternative (add encrypt-then-MAC to BaseEncryptionManager) changes the wire format and breaks interop with older peers

rejecting StaticMembershipInterceptor/TcpPingInterceptor beneath EncryptInterceptor (extending EncryptInterceptor.java:89) breaks configurations that are valid today and that StaticMembershipInterceptor.java:166-184 expects (failure detector/ping below it)

fairness_risks: Documented OFB/CFB support (cluster-interceptor.xml:221-223; TestEncryptInterceptor.java:164-190): a rule saying 'all modes must be authenticated' contradicts these tests unless the hidden tests are rewritten.
Changing the default algorithm or adding a MAC changes the wire format: mixed-version clusters stop interoperating, and a hidden test pinned to one wire layout would be unfair.
The plaintext control frames under T4 are constant markers; a hidden test that demands they be encrypted needs a stated rule, otherwise rejecting the configuration is just as defensible.

design.why: Best available design: T1 (advisory default, easy anchor) + T2 (second implementation behind documented opt-in modes, both-type) + T3 (short-frame shape, mimo-type) + T4 (producer below the interceptor, deepseek-type). It is not recommended: T1 and T2 collapse into one group under the cleanest fix (authenticate in BaseEncryptionManager or allow AEAD only); T3 and T4 are only loosely related to CWE-311; and T2 and T4 carry real fairness conflicts with existing tests and configurations. That leaves at most 2 defensible independent security groups, below the 3-trap bar.
